codeTemplate.scala: object Main extends App {\n  println("Hello, Scala!")\n}

steps.title: Print numbers 1 to N
steps.description: Write a for loop that prints the numbers from 1 to 20 to the console, each on its own line. This establishes the basic loop structure.
hints: Use a for loop: for (let i = 1; i <= 20; i++)
Test that numbers 1 through 20 are printed

verification.failureMessage: Make sure you print each number from 1 to 20.

steps.title: Fizz for multiples of 3
steps.description: Modify the loop to print "Fizz" instead of the number when the current number is divisible by 3.
hints: Use if (i % 3 === 0) to check divisibility by 3
Print "Fizz" for multiples of 3, otherwise print the number

steps.title: Buzz for multiples of 5
steps.description: Add a condition to print "Buzz" when the number is divisible by 5. Make sure the order of conditions is correct.
hints: Use else if (i % 5 === 0) for multiples of 5
Check divisibility by 3 FIRST, then by 5

steps.title: FizzBuzz for both
steps.description: Add a condition that prints "FizzBuzz" when a number is divisible by BOTH 3 and 5. This check must come first!
hints: Check i % 3 === 0 && i % 5 === 0 as the FIRST condition
15 is the first number divisible by both 3 and 5

verification.successMessage: FizzBuzz appears for numbers divisible by both!
verification.failureMessage: 15 should show FizzBuzz, not Fizz or Buzz.

steps.title: Refactor as a function
steps.description: Refactor the logic into a reusable function fizzbuzz(n) that returns the result for a single number, then call it from a loop.
hints: The function should return "FizzBuzz", "Fizz", "Buzz", or the number as a string
Using a function makes the code reusable and testable

verification.failureMessage: Create a fizzbuzz function and use it in a loop.
